label: Flowery
_selectorVarNote: selectorVar is DELIBERATELY OMITTED even though the dispatcher really does switch on `myattackchoice`. Reason, verified by running gen_attacks.js's own attackAnnouncements() against gml_Object_obj_flowery_enemy_Step_0.gml: the file yields 24 announcements, and the FIRST one is the intro dash tutorial at Step_0:512, whose enclosing `if` is `if (introtimer == 21)` (Step_0:510). The scanner therefore records that row as selector "introtimer", choice 21. If selectorVar were set, gen_attacks.js's RECONCILE pass (`byChoice.get(Number(a.choice))`) would match that row against this file's choice-21 entry — AquaKnives — and rewrite its name to "AquaKnives" and its type from 637 to 641. Dedupe would then collapse it with the genuine AquaKnives row (same controller/type/name) and KEEP the intro row, so launching AquaKnives would replay the intro branch: `dc.type = 637; scr_turntimer(9999999); introcon = 2;`. With selectorVar absent the reconcile loop `continue`s, every scanned row keeps its own selector/choice, and the REAL filter still works because it prefers `realTypes` (all 23 deduped entries carry a type). Cost of the omission: none — the scanner already writes selector "myattackchoice" onto the 23 dispatcher rows by itself, which is what the box block needs.

The block ends with `global.mnfight = 2; scr_turntimer(90);` written TWICE (Step_0:1177-1178 and 1192-1193) — a verbatim duplicated paragraph in the source, harmless because scr_turntimer only raises.

turnBlock._verified: extractTurnBlock() run against the real file: the anchor occurs twice (Step_0:1178 and 1193), the first passes the /turntimer/ proximity test on its own text, and the endAnchor (3 occurrences: 506, 1165, 1180) resolves to the 1180 one because indexOf starts at `at`. turnBlock._note: Flowery has NO turn-length ladder. Every per-attack length lives INSIDE its own dispatcher branch (`scr_turntimer(320)` / `(3200)` / `(3800)` / `(9999)` / `(9999999)`, Step_0:1223-1399) and therefore rides along in each entry's `setup` slice. The only shared statement is this 90-frame floor, which runs before any choice test. Anchoring the turn block on the dispatcher instead would slice the entire 180-line if-chain and spawn a second obj_dbulletcontroller — the Knight bug. IMPORTANT: the big numbers are CEILINGS, not durations. Flowery's attacks terminate THEMSELVES by writing global.turntimer directly when their pattern finishes: obj_orangeheart_floweryjarona_Step_0.gml:359-360 (`battle_timer > 315 && mode != 4` -> 5), :1190 (deflected with no bullets -> 30), :1379 (deflected into the bullet fan -> 90); obj_debug_orangeheartcontroller_Step_0.gml:76 (walls tutorial reaches the jump pad -> 70), :514 (the give-up dialogue -> 5), :583 (wall_counter 6 cleared -> 15); obj_orangeheart_wall_Create_0.gml:174 (tutorial wall 4 -> 9999, an extension). A studio that honours only the dispatcher number will sit on an empty box for 3200 frames (~107 s at 30 fps) after the attack visibly ends.

cut.name: OrbitStars
cut.evidence: Step_0:1394-1400. No writer. The highest type in the file and the only one that sets `rotatecontrol = true` on obj_orangeheart (obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:4916-4945), which repurposes up/down to spin obj_orangeheart_bullet_orbit instead of moving the soul (obj_orangeheart_Step_0.gml:28-40) — a whole input mode that ships unused.

mechanics: ORANGE SOUL, start to finish. Flowery is monstertype 119 / encounter 225 (scr_encountersetup.gml:872-878): HP 7000, AT 16, DF 0, mercymax 100, base ACTs Check / Posey 160 TP / PoseyZ 125 TP (scr_monstersetup.gml:581-611). He CANNOT be killed — the moment `global.monsterhp <= 99% of max` during enemytalk the fight interrupts into the healing scene (Step_0:569-580) which ends with `global.monsterhp[myself] = global.monstermaxhp[myself];` (Step_0:3532), up to three times (global.flag[1873]). The fight is won on MERCY only. Every bullet turn is played as obj_orangeheart: up/down move 8 px (obj_orangeheart_Step_0.gml:18-84, with per-attack y clamps against scr_get_box, obj_orangeheart_square boxes and the tutorial clamp), and hold the confirm button to charge then release to DASH forward (obj_orangeheart_Step_0.gml:86-230, chargecon 0->5, maxcharge 10, chargedistance 60), while obj_debug_orangeheartcontroller scrolls the world left at fakecamxspeedbase -16 (or -8 for the box attacks) and generates walls, chasers, bounce balls and word gates ahead of you. The soul is never green/purple/yellow and never the plain red heart; obj_heart is hidden by every type branch. PHASE LADDER, all mercy-gated (Step_0:354-489) with a per-phase mercy cap (_maxmercy at Step_0:8-24): phase 1 -> 2 at mercymod 10, 2 -> 3 at 20, 3 -> 4 at 30, 4 -> 5 at 40, 5 -> 6 at 50, 6 -> 7 at 80. Each transition calls event_user(0) (Other_10.gml) which REPLACES the ACT menu: phase 2 BlowAway 160 / BlowAwayZ 125 (a button-mash, Step_0:1708-1766 -> acting 101, presscount_1 capped at 5, presstimer, progress decay 0.2/frame); phase 3 Spin 200 / SpinZ 160; phase 4 Praise 200 / PraiseZ 160; phase 5 Justice 250, which is NOT an ACT at all but the Ace-Attorney trial minigame — Step_0:2599-2620 creates obj_yellow_trial_manager with trial_id 99, flowery_mode true and a three-item evidence list (Metal Cuff / Moss / Prisoncloth); phase 6 SusiesIdea 120, which is the finale trigger. `NOOO_MERCY` (Create_0.gml:36, set true at each transition and cleared when the new enemies finish entering, Step_0:4143/4162/4186/4197) gates mercy payout during the entrances. TENSION is the fuel: breaking walls and touching helpful flowers pays scr_tensionheal scaled by `moar_tension`, which ramps 1.0 -> 1.5 with global.tempflag[74] (the retry counter) at Step_0:46-65 and is read in obj_orangeheart_helpful_flower_Create_0.gml:28, obj_orangeheart_wall_Create_0.gml:96 and obj_orangeheart_wall_Step_0.gml:58 — the anti-frustration lever. CAST: obj_flowery_enemy is the only obj_monsterparent. Aqua, Seth (purple), Orange, Green, Blue and Yellow are obj_flowery_marker props created in Create_0.gml:198-235 and walked on-screen by the aqua_and_purple_enter / green_and_orange_enter / yellow_and_blue_enter state machines (Step_0:4141-4279) at phases 3, 4 and 5; their aqua_mercy / purple_mercy / ... counters are display-only. obj_flowery_towery is the shader-rendered rotating tower the whole fight stands on. PHASE 5 -> 6 IS NOT PURELY MERCY: obj_yellow_trial_manager_Create_0.gml:729-740 does `with (obj_flowery_enemy) { succeed_trial_count++; if (succeed_trial_count == 2) phase = 6; }` — two cleared trials jump the phase directly. PHASE 7 IS DEAD: Step_0:483-489 sets phase = 7 and phasetransition_con = 20, and nothing anywhere tests phasetransition_con == 20, so the turn loop (gated on phasetransition_con == 0 at Step_0:582/1107/1110) simply stops. It is unreachable in normal play anyway — phase 6's only ACTs are Check and SusiesIdea, so mercymod cannot climb to 80 without the debug 'P' key (Step_0:72-97). Likewise endcon: mercymod >= 100 sets endcon 1 (Step_0:566-567) which becomes endcon 2 after 30 frames (Step_0:4037-4045) and then nothing — there is no scr_wincombat in this fight. THE FINALE. Phase 6, SusiesIdea: Step_0:2665-2988. acting 2 -> a Susie/Flowery dialogue chain (2.11 .. 2.14, or straight to 2.91 on a retry via global.flag[1874]) -> acting 2.91 makes obj_marker, obj_flowery_hero_flower, obj_flowery_marker, obj_heroparent, obj_battlecontroller, obj_tensionbar, obj_flowery_throwkris, obj_flowery_enemy, obj_flowery_towery and obj_flowery_tower_decoration persistent for 5 frames, calls `room_goto(room_dw_fcastle_flowerclimb)` (Step_0:2840) and then hand-shifts every one of them by (-last_cam_x, 11640 - last_cam_y) so the battle scene lands at the bottom of the 11 000-pixel climb room (Step_0:2841-2914). obj_flowery_enemy_Other_4 (Room Start) un-persists them all again. acting 2.92 spawns obj_flowery_throwkris on Susie, at acttimer 32 forces throwcon = 2 and throws a spr_kris_jump_ball marker upward, calls obj_dw_fcastle_flowerclimb.start_pan(), hides the battle UI and at acttimer 100 destroys obj_monsterparent / obj_bulletparent / obj_tensionbar, clears global.fighting and destroys obj_battlecontroller. STAGE 2 — THE CLIMB (obj_dw_fcastle_flowerclimb, Create_0 29 lines + Step_0 176 lines): start_pan() puts obj_mainchara at x = -300 in cutscene mode, scr_losechar(), destroys the followers; the Step then lerps the camera to y 9466 over 120 frames while a spr_kris_dw_plummet marker flies up at vspeed -14, flips to spr_plat_kris_ball with gravity 0.9 once it passes the obj_climbstarter, and on the way back down becomes obj_climb_kris (Step_0:139-158). Kris then climbs the rotating tower under obj_rotating_tower_controller_new. Input contract (obj_climb_kris_Step_0.gml:90-230): hold a DIRECTION to grab hand-over-hand — with a directional buffer of `ceil(5 - climbmomentum*2)` frames, a slip state that punishes reversing into the direction you were just bumped from (:186-196), and momentum/boost that make the buffer shorter as you speed up — plus HOLD the jump button to charge (chargetime1 10, chargetime2 22) and release to leap. The climb is a chained BOOST run: the room places eleven obj_climb_boostenemy with boost_bonus 1..11 (gml_RoomCC_room_dw_fcastle_flowerclimb_8/9/16..24_PreCreate.gml); hitting one mid-jump launches Kris `600 + 20 * boost_bonus` pixels upward (obj_climb_kris_Step_0.gml:381-394) so each successive hit throws you higher. Three obj_plat_cam_clampzone areas (extflag area_1/2/3) re-wrap the climbables around the cylinder as you pass them (obj_dw_fcastle_flowerclimb_Step_0.gml:56-107); the `end` trigger fades out and does `room_goto(room_dw_fcastle_flowerydash)` (:20-43). STAGE 3 — THE RUN + PARRY (obj_dw_flowerydash + obj_plat_finalflowery). obj_dw_flowerydash_Step_0.gml:7-171 plays the cutscene where Flowery absorbs the six flowers, then con 10 turns the game into a platform-mode AUTO-RUNNER: obj_plat_player gets `dashing = true; static_dash = true; static_dash_fake_speed = 24` (:273-283) and the parallax and floor scroll at dashspeed 24, while `instance_create(480, 160, obj_plat_finalflowery)` (:242) brings in OMEGA FLOWERY. obj_plat_finalflowery has hp 100 and a con machine (Step_0:7-13): 6 INTRO, 0 IDLE, 2 JARONA, 3 FINALJARONA, and the unreachable 1 BULLETS / 4 ACTING / 5 FLATTER. Because `only_jarona = true` (Create_0.gml:88 and :424, never cleared) IDLE always routes to JARONA (Step_0:50-52) and BULLETS is dead. JARONA is the PARRY loop: subcon 0 charges for 80 frames with rainbow bwooshes; subcon 1 picks a random rona voice clip and waits ronawait frames; subcon 2 dashes him leftward across the screen carrying `dashbullet`, an obj_plat_bulletred whose damage is `min(floor(hp*0.4) + df, hp - 1 + df, 60 + df)` (Step_0:179-189) — it can never kill you outright; subcon 9 resets him to xstart. The player must land the platform-mode slash (obj_plat_hbx, generated by obj_plat_player_Step_0.gml:1654-1690) on him as he passes: Collision_obj_plat_hbx destroys the dashbullet, adds 1.7 to attack_speed, cycles the sunset colour and switch_subcon(9). Missing costs progress — passing off-screen left does `jarona_repeat--` (Step_0:237-238). jarona_repeat_target is 8 (Step_0:69-77), and `is_final_jarona = jarona_repeat == jarona_repeat_target - 1` (:131), forced early if Kris is below 2 HP (:133-134). On the final pass act_enabled is switched OFF, attack_speed drops to 18 and memory = 2 so he homes onto the player's y (:138-144, :204-205); contact (or a hit) goes to con 3. FINALJARONA is the clash: subcon 0 freezes Kris in spr_kris_plat_clash, kills the music, spawns obj_screen_zoom; subcon 1 pushes the ghost line three times (subcontimer 1/31/51) and at subcontimer 131 sets `qte_prompt_state = 1`. That raises the PARRY BAR (drawn by the press_ui marker in Create_0.gml:18-86 out of spr_pressfront / spr_pressspot / spr_attackspot) and starts boltframe counting: pressing button1, button2 OR button3 while `boltframe > 60 && boltframe < 110` (Step_0:806-828) is a SUCCESS -> subcon 2, Kris slashes through, global.flag[1852] = 2; letting boltframe reach 110 is a FAIL -> subcon 3, Flowery punches Kris, global.flag[1852] = 1. Either way global.plot = 499, scr_setparty(1,1) and room_goto(room_dw_post_flowery_battle) (Step_0:526-535 / :676-685). There is no death state in stage 3 — the outcome is a flag, not a game over.
